title: Tigers set Verlander's farewell start for September 26 vs. Pirates
dek: The Detroit Tigers announced that Justin Verlander will start Saturday, September 26, against the Pittsburgh Pirates in what is likely his final career start. The 43-year-old Hall of Famer, sidelined by hip and hamstring injuries since March 30, will return after a successful bullpen session on Tuesday.
author: The GoCheckMySports Desk
key_fact: Justin Verlander's scheduled final start is Saturday, September 26, versus the Pittsburgh Pirates after injuries have kept him out since March 30.
bottom_line: Verlander's start on September 26 will determine whether this becomes an official farewell or mark a change in his retirement plans. The injury status that allowed him to throw Tuesday, and his tolerance for that workload, will frame how much of an appearance he can make.
body: The Detroit Tigers announced that Justin Verlander will take the mound Saturday, September 26, against the Pittsburgh Pirates in what is likely his final career start before retiring.

Verlander, 43, has been sidelined by hip and hamstring injuries since March 30. After a bullop session went well Tuesday afternoon, the Tigers scheduled his return for the weekend matchup. According to CBS Sports reporting, Verlander is not expected to pitch a full game and could throw just one inning, similar to Charlie Morton's farewell appearance with the Atlanta Braves last season.

Saturday's start will mark Verlander's 557th career start, the 29th most in MLB history, per Yahoo Sports reporting. Over 21 MLB seasons, Verlander compiled a 266-159 record with a 3.33 ERA and 3,554 strikeouts, placing him eighth on the all-time strikeout list. He is a three-time Cy Young Award winner, an MVP, and a two-time World Series champion.

Verlander announced his retirement in July, when he was named to the All-Star Game as a Legends Pick. In remarks ahead of this weekend, he said: "We're not following the normal script for rehab players. I mean, there's no point. I told these guys: 'What are we saving my arm for?' It doesn't make a lot of sense. I think clearly there's some underlying stuff there with the hamstring, but it just is what it is. I mean, there's a chance that I could seriously hurt myself, but it's part of being a professional athlete at 43."

Both the Tigers and their weekend opponent, the Pirates, have already been eliminated from postseason contention, clearing the way for a farewell moment untethered to playoff pressure. The Tigers have announced plans for farewell events celebrating the pitcher's career.
